newsitem.title: USA: Court denies Haft rehearing on control of Dart.
newsitem.headline: Court denies Haft rehearing on control of Dart.

text.p: WILMINGTON, April 1 (Reuter) A Delaware judge has denied a request by Hebert Haft for a rehearing on his lawsuit to regain control of the Dart Group Corp.

In a decision released today, Chancellor William Allen of the Delaware Chancery Court said there were no legal or factual errors in his March 14 ruling rejecting Haft's claim that he has the right to vote a controlling block of Dart shares.
Haft has challenged a settlement between Dart and his estranged son Ronald to whom Herbert sold the controlling shares while retaining an "irrevocable proxy" to vote them.
In a statement last month, Dart said it hoped the court's ruling "may help it reach a negotiated settlement with Herbert Haft" rather than have to go to trial.

Without a settlement, the Dart Group faces two trials: one with Herbert and one with his former wife Gloria and two of their three children, Robert and Linda. Both suits are in the Chancery Court and both seek control of Dart.
Dart is a retail holding company based in Landover, Maryland.
